doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Met orchestra and joining CTI
title: Choosing material for Afro-Classic with Creed Taylor and Don Sebesky
summary: Laws describes choosing the Bach Passacaglia, Love Story, a Mozart sonata and Fire and Rain, with Creed Taylor's suggestions and Sebesky's arrangements.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Let’s go back in the chronology. We’re going to get – for me, this is – critics, they loved this one. For me – but I want you to talk about this, because this is . . .

Well, I remember being up there in the office with Don Sebesky and Creed. We were deciding on material to record. So we decided on the Bach Passacaglia, and I think the theme from Love Story is on there.

That was Creed’s input, because Creed always liked to bridge the gap between the average theatergoer and the music. He always looked for something – I think Crying Song was also the same thing. So that was one of the things he and I talked about when

we were on tour last year in Europe. He always – he’s always producing. Even during the show, he’s trying to bring quality to our performances, live performances. So he was the one that chose Love Story, because that film was out with what’s-her­ name?

Ryan O’Neal, and what’s that other girl’s name? But anyway, it was strong. It was a strong movie. So he thought that would be a good idea. So he used that as a bridge. And I think we did a Mozart piece.
Um-hmm. The flute sonata in F.

At the time, it was very intriguing. I thought it also displayed the flute well. Fire and Rain is also – I think it was one of Creed’s suggestions. Don Sebesky was the one, I think, who did the arrangement on that.
